title: Introduce RAG scenarios CLI authoring kit and local runner
author: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: engineers onboarding to RAG workflows still spend time wiring together ad-hoc prompts, local runners, and smoke assertions. There is no small CLI-first kit that combines authoring templates, stepwise assertions, and a compact local playback runner for iterative development.

Solution: introduce a small CLI tool (ragctl) plus a set of opinionated scenario templates and devcontainer samples to speed up developer iteration. The kit focuses on: 1) a compact scenario JSON/YAML format with explicit steps and inline assertions, 2) a local playback runner that can operate headless or with a small web UI for step-by-step inspection, 3) scaffolding templates (TS/Python) for tool stubs and mock connectors, and 4) telemetry probes and simple automatic snapshot assertions for regressions.

What this PR contains: added ragctl CLI (Go, compiled binary in repo for dev), three scenario template families (faq-assistant, multi-turn-qa, and tool-calling), a lightweight scenario runner implemented in TypeScript (node) that replays steps against the Redwood hosted API or local stubbed runtime, docs site quickstart pages, a devcontainer for consistent local debugging, TypeScript and Python example tool stubs, and a small test harness that can assert token-level/semantic invariants.

Usage summary: `ragctl init` scaffolds a new scenario folder; `ragctl run --scenario ./scenarios/sample.json --target=hosted` will run against hosted Redwood API; `ragctl run --scenario ./scenarios/sample.json --target=local --stub` runs against local mock tools. Templates include `--assert` annotations usable for CI smoke checks. The quickstart docs include an example CI job snippet for GitHub Actions that runs the scenario runner and fails the build on assertion mismatch.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for the scenario parser and assertion engine, e2e smoke that runs the sample scenario against a local mock API (CI stage `scenario-smoke`). Performance: runner is intentionally single-process and streaming-friendly; initial runs of the sample scenario finish in ~1.2s on developer laptop.

Checklist: - [x] CLI scaffolding and commands implemented - [x] Scenario format documented - [x] 3 example templates added (faq-assistant, multi-turn-qa, tool-calling) - [x] TypeScript runner + local webstep inspector - [x] Python/TS tool stubs - [x] Devcontainer and quickstart docs - [x] CI smoke job and test coverage - [x] Telemetry probe hooks (optional runtime integration)

Why this is different from existing quickstarts: instead of larger microservice starters or full RAG stacks, this kit is minimal by design — intended for rapid authoring and CI-based regression checks for RAG prompt/eval drift. It intentionally avoids heavy infra and focuses on developer-loop velocity.

References: linear tasks ENG-2149, docs story PM-672; related PRs include local-runner experiments and existing quickstart telemetry guidelines.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the scenario schema (schema/v1.md) and the assertion semantics (inline vs snapshot). I want sign-off on the CI snippet format since teams will copy it into product repos. If you'd like the CLI to support additional output formats (junit/ndjson) I can add that in a follow-up.
